byte-size-calculator.quickAnswer: Type a byte count and this tool shows it in every common unit at once. Decimal units use powers of 1,000 (1 KB = 1,000 bytes) while binary units use powers of 1,024 (1 KiB = 1,024 bytes). Example: 1,048,576 bytes = 1.048576 MB but exactly 1 MiB.
keyFacts: SI/decimal units (KB, MB, GB) use powers of 1,000. They are the standard for storage makers and networks.
Binary units (KiB, MiB, GiB) use powers of 1,024 and are the standard for RAM and most operating systems.
This 1,000 vs 1,024 split is why a "1 TB" drive shows as about 931 GiB in your OS.
1 byte = 8 bits. Network speeds in Mbps (megabits) are 8× the MB/s (megabytes) download figure.
The KiB/MiB/GiB names were standardized by the IEC in 1998 to end the confusion.
Petabyte scale: 1 PB = 1,000 TB = 1,000,000 GB in decimal units.
howTo: Type the number of bytes in the input box.
The decimal table (KB, MB, GB, TB, PB) updates instantly.
The binary table (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB) updates at the same time.
Compare the two columns to see exactly where the 1,000 vs 1,024 difference bites.
byte-size-calculator.formula:
Decimal: value ÷ 1,000ⁿ (n = 1 for KB, 2 for MB, 3 for GB...).
Binary: value ÷ 1,024ⁿ (n = 1 for KiB, 2 for MiB, 3 for GiB...).
Example: 1,048,576 ÷ 1,000² = 1.048576 MB; 1,048,576 ÷ 1,024² = 1 MiB.
benefits: Both unit systems side by side - the confusion explained, not just converted.
Settles "missing storage" arguments: see why your 1 TB drive shows 931 GiB.
Handy for developers sizing buffers, uploads, and database fields.
No sign-up, instant results, works offline.
limitations: Input is bytes only - use the Data Storage Converter to convert between other unit pairs.
Negative values are treated as zero; sizes cannot be negative.
Extremely large values beyond petabytes are not shown.

faqs.q: What is the difference between MB and MiB?
faqs.a: MB (megabyte) is decimal: 1,000,000 bytes. MiB (mebibyte) is binary: 1,048,576 bytes (1,024²). Storage makers advertise in MB/GB; operating systems usually display MiB/GiB, which is why capacities look smaller than advertised.

faqs.q: Why does my 1 TB hard drive show as 931 GB?
faqs.a: The maker counts 1 TB as 1,000,000,000,000 bytes. Your OS divides by 1,024³ (1,073,741,824), giving 931.3 GiB, which it labels "GB". Nothing is missing - it is just two different units sharing one name.

faqs.q: How many bytes are in a kilobyte?
faqs.a: It depends: 1,000 bytes in the decimal/SI kilobyte (KB), 1,024 bytes in the binary kibibyte (KiB). In everyday speech "kilobyte" usually means 1,024 bytes, but storage and networking standards use 1,000.

faqs.q: Is a bit the same as a byte?
faqs.a: No. A bit is one binary digit (0 or 1); a byte is 8 bits. Internet speeds are sold in megabits per second (Mbps), so divide by 8 to get the megabytes-per-second download figure you actually feel.
Petabyte (PB): 1,000 TB decimal or 1,024 TiB binary. Then exabyte (EB), zettabyte (ZB), and yottabyte (YB) - each 1,000× the last in decimal.

faqs.q: Which unit should I use in my app?
faqs.a: Follow your platform: file sizes and disk space in decimal (KB/MB/GB) match what storage makers print; memory/RAM figures in binary (KiB/MiB/GiB) match what operating systems report. Label them clearly either way.

labels.note: Storage makers use decimal; operating systems usually display binary. That is why capacities look "smaller" than advertised.

mistakes: KB and KiB are not the same: 1 KB = 1,000 bytes but 1 KiB = 1,024 bytes. Read the column heading before quoting a number.
Your 'missing' drive space isn't missing — a 1 TB drive shows ~931 GiB because makers use decimal and your OS uses binary.
This tool takes bytes as input only. Typing '500 MB' into the bytes field gives nonsense — convert the value to bytes first.
Expecting the binary column to match the decimal one — 1,048,576 bytes reads 1.048576 MB but exactly 1 MiB. The gap is the point, not an error.
RAM is measured in binary (GiB) but storage is sold in decimal (GB). Comparing a 16 GB phone with 16 GiB of RAM mixes two rulers.
